Tendon sheath of extensor digitorum and.displayName: Right Tendon sheath of extensor digitorum and extensor indicis
Tendon sheath of extensor digitorum and.baseName: Tendon sheath of extensor digitorum and extensor indicis
Tendon sheath of extensor digitorum and.description:
TENDON SHEATH OF EXTENSOR DIGITORUM AND EXTENSOR INDICIS

This tendon sheath is a synovial sheath that encloses the four tendons of extensor digitorum together with the tendon of extensor indicis within the fourth dorsal compartment of the wrist, ulnar to the extensor pollicis longus compartment.

== Function ==

It allows the extensor digitorum and extensor indicis tendons to glide together with minimal friction as they extend the fingers and index finger at the metacarpophalangeal joints.

== Clinical relevance ==

This compartment is a common site of tenosynovitis in rheumatoid arthritis, where synovial proliferation can weaken and eventually rupture the extensor tendons.

Tendon sheath of extensor digitorum and.displayName: Left Tendon sheath of extensor digitorum and extensor indicis
Tendon sheath of extensor digitorum and.baseName: Tendon sheath of extensor digitorum and extensor indicis
Tendon sheath of extensor digitorum and.description:
TENDON SHEATH OF EXTENSOR DIGITORUM AND EXTENSOR INDICIS

Tendon sheath of tibialis anterior.r.displayName: Right Tendon sheath of tibialis anterior
Tendon sheath of tibialis anterior.r.description:
TENDON SHEATH OF TIBIALIS ANTERIOR

The tendon sheath of tibialis anterior is a synovial sheath enclosing the tibialis anterior tendon as it passes beneath the superior and inferior extensor retinacula at the front of the ankle, extending from just above the ankle joint to approximately the talonavicular joint.

== Function ==

It reduces friction and prevents bowstringing of the tibialis anterior tendon as it crosses the ankle during dorsiflexion and inversion of the foot.

== Clinical relevance ==

Tenosynovitis of this sheath can cause anterior ankle pain and swelling and may be associated with overuse or inflammatory arthropathy.

Tendon sheath of extensor hallucis longu.displayName: Right Tendon sheath of extensor hallucis longus
Tendon sheath of extensor hallucis longu.baseName: Tendon sheath of extensor hallucis longus
Tendon sheath of extensor hallucis longu.description:
TENDON SHEATH OF EXTENSOR HALLUCIS LONGUS

The tendon sheath of extensor hallucis longus is a synovial sheath enclosing the extensor hallucis longus tendon, beginning slightly above the ankle joint (proximal to the tibialis anterior sheath's distal end) and extending to the base of the first metatarsal, deep to the extensor retinacula.

== Function ==

It reduces friction as the tendon crosses the ankle and dorsum of the foot during extension of the great toe and dorsiflexion of the ankle.

== Clinical relevance ==

It lies close to the anterior tibial artery and deep fibular nerve at the ankle, and tenosynovitis here can accompany anterior ankle impingement or overuse injuries.

Tendon sheath of extensor digitorum long.displayName: Right Tendon sheath of extensor digitorum longus
Tendon sheath of extensor digitorum long.baseName: Tendon sheath of extensor digitorum longus
Tendon sheath of extensor digitorum long.description:
TENDON SHEATH OF EXTENSOR DIGITORUM LONGUS

The tendon sheath of extensor digitorum longus is a synovial sheath that encloses the tendons of extensor digitorum longus, together with the tendon of fibularis tertius, as they pass beneath the extensor retinacula at the ankle before diverging toward the lateral four toes.

== Function ==

It reduces friction and allows the extensor digitorum longus tendons to glide as a group during dorsiflexion of the ankle and extension of the toes.

== Clinical relevance ==

This sheath can be involved in anterior ankle tenosynovitis, often related to repetitive dorsiflexion activities such as running.

Tendon sheath of flexor digitorum longus.displayName: Right Tendon sheath of flexor digitorum longus
Tendon sheath of flexor digitorum longus.baseName: Tendon sheath of flexor digitorum longus
Tendon sheath of flexor digitorum longus.description:
TENDON SHEATH OF FLEXOR DIGITORUM LONGUS

The tendon sheath of flexor digitorum longus is a synovial sheath enclosing the flexor digitorum longus tendon as it passes through the tarsal tunnel behind the medial malleolus, deep to the flexor retinaculum, positioned anterior to the flexor hallucis longus and posterior to the tibialis posterior tendon.

== Function ==

It reduces friction as the tendon curves around the medial malleolus en route to the plantar surface of the lesser toes.

== Clinical relevance ==

Along with the tibialis posterior and flexor hallucis longus sheaths, it lies within the tarsal tunnel and can contribute to posteromedial ankle pain in tarsal tunnel syndrome.

Tendon sheath of tibialis posterior musc.displayName: Right Tendon sheath of tibialis posterior muscle
Tendon sheath of tibialis posterior musc.baseName: Tendon sheath of tibialis posterior muscle
Tendon sheath of tibialis posterior musc.description:
TENDON SHEATH OF TIBIALIS POSTERIOR MUSCLE

The tendon sheath of tibialis posterior muscle is a synovial sheath enclosing the tibialis posterior tendon as it travels deep to the flexor retinaculum along the medial aspect of the ankle, positioned most anteriorly of the three tarsal tunnel tendons.

== Function ==

It reduces friction and allows the tibialis posterior tendon to glide smoothly around the medial malleolus during inversion and plantarflexion of the foot, and while supporting the medial longitudinal arch.

== Clinical relevance ==

Tenosynovitis and progressive dysfunction of this tendon within its sheath are a leading cause of acquired adult flatfoot deformity.

Tendon sheath of flexor hallucis longus..baseName: Tendon sheath of flexor hallucis longus
Tendon sheath of flexor hallucis longus..description:
TENDON SHEATH OF FLEXOR HALLUCIS LONGUS

The tendon sheath of flexor hallucis longus is a synovial sheath enclosing the flexor hallucis longus tendon as it passes through the tarsal tunnel behind the medial malleolus, most posterior of the three flexor tendons, then curves beneath the sustentaculum tali toward the great toe.

== Function ==

It reduces friction as the tendon changes direction sharply around the posterior talus and sustentaculum tali during flexion of the great toe.

== Clinical relevance ==

This sheath is classically affected in 'dancer's tendinitis,' an overuse tenosynovitis common in ballet dancers due to repetitive demi-pointe and full-pointe positions.

Common tendon sheath of fibularis muscle.displayName: Right Common tendon sheath of fibularis muscles
Common tendon sheath of fibularis muscle.baseName: Common tendon sheath of fibularis muscles
Common tendon sheath of fibularis muscle.description:
COMMON TENDON SHEATH OF FIBULARIS MUSCLES

The common tendon sheath of the fibularis (peroneal) muscles is a synovial sheath that encloses the tendons of fibularis longus and fibularis brevis together as they pass posterior to the lateral malleolus, held in place by the superior fibular retinaculum.

== Function ==

It allows both fibularis tendons to glide as a unit around the lateral malleolus during eversion and plantarflexion of the foot.

== Clinical relevance ==

Tenosynovitis or subluxation of the fibularis tendons from this sheath (peroneal tendon instability) commonly follows lateral ankle sprains.

Common tendon sheath of fibularis muscle.displayName: Left Common tendon sheath of fibularis muscles
Common tendon sheath of fibularis muscle.baseName: Common tendon sheath of fibularis muscles

Plantar tendon sheath of fibularis longu.displayName: Right Plantar tendon sheath of fibularis longus muscle
Plantar tendon sheath of fibularis longu.baseName: Plantar tendon sheath of fibularis longus muscle
Plantar tendon sheath of fibularis longu.description:
PLANTAR TENDON SHEATH OF FIBULARIS LONGUS MUSCLE

The plantar tendon sheath of fibularis longus muscle is a separate synovial sheath that encloses the fibularis longus tendon as it crosses the sole of the foot, from the region of the cuboid bone to its insertion on the base of the first metatarsal and medial cuneiform.

== Function ==

It reduces friction as the tendon turns around the cuboid groove and crosses the plantar surface of the foot, supporting the transverse arch and assisting plantarflexion and eversion.

== Clinical relevance ==

This sheath is distinct from the common fibularis sheath at the ankle and can be a site of plantar lateral foot pain in fibularis longus tendinopathy.
